# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/config-reference.mjs from the schema. Edit scripts/docs/config-descriptions.json, then run: node scripts/docs/config-reference.mjs --write -->

Every setting `rigour.yml` accepts: 210 in all, generated from the schema Rigour validates the file with, so a default here is the default the code uses. Most teams change only a few of them; [Configuration](./CONFIGURATION.md) says which, and how settings combine.

A setting you leave out takes its default. A setting this page does not list is ignored.

## Top level

File-wide settings: the template labels rigour init applied, and the paths every check skips.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string | none | Names the role template rigour init applied; it is shown in scan output and audit exports and does not change any check at run time. |
| `paradigm` | string | none | Names the coding-paradigm template rigour init applied; it is shown in scan output and fix packets and does not change any check at run time. |
| `brief.enabled` | boolean | `true` | The kill switch for briefings: false stops the prompt hook, rigour brief and rigour_brief alike. The prompt hook itself is installed only with rigour hooks init --brief; RIGOUR_BRIEF=0 stops briefings for one person. |
| `brief.max_items` | number | `10` | The most items a briefing gives, between 1 and 10. |
| `learning.outcomes.mode` | "off" \| "on" \| "required" | `"off"` | Reads what happened after each pull request merged (CI on its merge commit, later commits and fixes on its files, a revert) with rigour outcomes: off, on, or required, which stops a person, RIGOUR_OUTCOMES or --no-outcomes turning it off (team; a person sets outcomes in settings.json). |
| `learning.outcomes.window_days` | number | `30` | How many days after a merge later commits on its files count, from 7 to 90; a record is settled once its window has closed and CI has an answer. |
| `learning.outcomes.demote_after` | number | `2` | How many later pull requests, from more than one author or merged at least a week apart, that a review found repeating a lesson and that then settled clean (CI passed, no fix on its file, no revert) take back a lesson an outcome or recurrence promoted; at least 2. |
| `ignore` | list of string | `[]` | Glob patterns for files every check, review and agent hook skips. |

## Project commands

`commands`

Your own format, lint, type-check and test commands. Before a push, each replaces the tool Rigour would otherwise find in node_modules and run on the changed files; `rigour check` runs them too. Each runs as written, on the whole project, without a shell: pipes and `&&` are not interpreted, so point at a script for those.

**Blocks:** A command that exits non-zero blocks the push and fails `rigour check`.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | string | none | Runs instead of the Prettier check of changed files; unset, Rigour uses what the project has installed. |
| `lint` | string | none | Runs instead of ESLint on changed files; unset, Rigour uses what the project has installed. |
| `typecheck` | string | none | Runs instead of the type check (the project's typecheck or check script, svelte-check or tsc); unset, Rigour uses what the project has installed. |
| `test` | string | none | Runs instead of the tests that import changed files (vitest related); unset, Rigour uses what the project has installed. |

## General

`gates`

Repository-wide checks for file length, placeholder comments and required documents. Teams change these to match their own size limits and documentation layout.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_file_lines` | number | `500` | Maximum number of lines a file may have before it is reported as too long; the same limit is checked on every edit, and 0 turns the full-repository check off. |
| `forbid_todos` | boolean | `true` | When on, comments that start with TODO are reported, outside test files and examples. |
| `forbid_fixme` | boolean | `true` | When on, comments that start with FIXME are reported, outside test files and examples. |
| `required_files` | list of string | see below | Files, relative to the repository root, that must exist; each one missing is reported, and an empty list turns the check off. |

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.required_files</code></summary>

```json
[
  "docs/SPEC.md",
  "docs/ARCH.md",
  "docs/DECISIONS.md",
  "docs/TASKS.md"
]
```

</details>

## Structure and complexity

`gates.ast`

Per-function and per-class limits checked by parsing JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and other supported languages. Teams raise or lower them to match how large they let functions and classes grow.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `complexity` | number | `10` | Maximum cyclomatic complexity per function (for Go, Rust, Java, C# and Ruby, a nesting-weighted complexity score); functions above it are reported. |
| `max_methods` | number | `10` | Maximum number of methods in one class in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python; larger classes are reported. |
| `max_params` | number | `5` | Maximum number of parameters per function in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python; functions with more are reported. |

## Legacy syntax

`gates.staleness`

Flags outdated JavaScript and TypeScript syntax such as var. Off by default; teams turn it on while modernising a codebase.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns legacy-syntax checks on JavaScript and TypeScript files on or off. |
| `rules` | map of boolean | see below | Per-rule switches for legacy-syntax checks; only no-var, no-commonjs (require calls) and no-arguments are checked, and a rule left out of the map is on while staleness is enabled. |

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.staleness.rules</code></summary>

```json
{
  "no-var": true,
  "no-commonjs": false,
  "no-arguments": false,
  "prefer-arrow": false,
  "prefer-template": false,
  "prefer-spread": false,
  "prefer-rest": false,
  "prefer-const": false
}
```

</details>

## Dependencies

`gates.dependencies`

Checks the root package.json (and Python, Go and Java manifests for forbidden packages) for banned, unused, heavy or overlapping dependencies. Teams change it to ban packages or quiet the unused-dependency check for side-effect imports.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forbid` | list of string | `[]` | Package names that must not appear in package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod or pom.xml; each one found is reported. |
| `detect_unused` | boolean | `true` | When on, package.json dependencies and devDependencies that no source or known config file imports or names are reported; common build tools and type packages are always skipped. |
| `detect_heavy_alternatives` | boolean | `true` | When on, package.json dependencies that have a known lighter alternative are reported with that alternative. |
| `detect_duplicate_purpose` | boolean | `true` | When on, two or more installed packages that serve the same purpose (for example two HTTP clients) are reported. |
| `unused_allowlist` | list of string | `[]` | Package names the unused-dependency check skips; a trailing * matches any name with that prefix. |

## Architecture boundaries

`gates.architecture`

Import rules between parts of the codebase, checked on JavaScript and TypeScript imports. Teams add rules to keep layers from importing each other.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boundaries` | list of object | `[]` | Import rules, each with from and to glob patterns and a mode; a deny rule reports any JavaScript or TypeScript file matching from that imports a path matching to, and allow rules have no effect. |

## Agent safety

`gates.safety`

Paths agents must not modify and a cap on how many files one agent cycle may change. Teams change it to protect CI, docs or config files that need human review.

**Blocks:** Advisory in review; the edit hook blocks the write (rigour setup installs it to block); rigour run stops on the file cap

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_files_changed_per_cycle` | number | `10` | Maximum number of files one agent command may change during rigour run before the run stops with a failure; it is also passed to the agent in the fix packet. |
| `protected_paths` | list of string | `[".github/**","docs/**","rigour.yml"]` | Path patterns agents must not modify; an edit to a matching path is reported by the edit hook and the MCP pattern check, and staged or modified matching files are reported by a full check. |

## Context drift

`gates.context`

Compares new code against conventions mined from the repository, such as environment variable names and naming style. Teams tune it when naming findings are too noisy or turn it off.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the context-drift check on or off, including the scan that mines project conventions it compares against. |
| `sensitivity` | number | `0.8` | A 0-1 ratio that sets how readily naming inconsistencies are reported: a casing style is reported when it is not the dominant one and accounts for more than (1 - sensitivity) of the names of that kind, so a higher value reports more. |
| `mining_depth` | number | `100` | Maximum number of files sampled to learn the project's environment variable names, which variants are then compared against. |

## Environment alignment

`gates.environment`

Checks that required tools are installed at the versions the project declares and that required environment variables are set. Teams pin tool versions or list variables their build needs.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the environment alignment check on or off. |
| `enforce_contracts` | boolean | `true` | When on, tool version ranges are also read from the project, Node from package.json engines and ruff and mypy from pyproject.toml, and checked against the installed tools. |
| `tools` | map of string | `{}` | Map of tool name to a semver range; each tool is run with --version and reported if missing or outside the range, and an entry overrides a range read from the project. |
| `required_env` | list of string | `[]` | Environment variable names that must be set in the environment Rigour runs in; each one unset is reported. |

## Retry loop breaker

`gates.retry_loop_breaker`

Reports when the same category of operation has failed repeatedly, telling the agent to stop retrying and read documentation. Teams change the retry limit or point categories at their own docs.

**Blocks:** Blocks: findings are critical

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the retry loop check on or off. |
| `max_retries` | number | `3` | Number of consecutive recorded failures in one category at which the loop is reported. |
| `doc_sources` | map of string | `{}` | Map of failure category to a documentation link or note shown in the finding instead of the built-in one. |

## Agent teams

`gates.agent_team`

Governs sessions where several agents work at once, limiting their number and overlapping task scopes. Off by default; teams turn it on when they run agents in parallel.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns agent team checks on or off; they apply only while a multi-agent session is registered. |
| `max_concurrent_agents` | number | `3` | Maximum number of agents registered in one session; more than this is reported. |
| `task_ownership` | "strict" \| "collaborative" | `"strict"` | In strict mode, two agents whose task scopes overlap are reported; collaborative mode allows overlap. |

## Checkpoints

`gates.checkpoint`

Checks the checkpoints an agent reports during long tasks for gaps, low quality scores and a declining trend. Off by default; teams turn it on for long-running supervised agent work.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns checkpoint checks on or off; they apply only once an agent has reported checkpoints. |
| `interval_minutes` | number | `15` | Expected minutes between checkpoints; a gap longer than twice this is reported. |
| `quality_threshold` | number | `80` | Minimum quality score, 0-100, for the latest checkpoint; a lower score is reported. |
| `drift_detection` | boolean | `true` | When on, a declining trend in checkpoint quality scores is reported. |

## Security patterns

`gates.security`

Scans source for injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal, hardcoded secrets, insecure randomness and similar vulnerabilities. Teams turn off a category that does not apply or change which severities are reported.

**Blocks:** Blocks a credential in a real secret's format; other patterns are notes unless block is on

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the security pattern check on or off for full checks, reviews and the push gate; the edit hook's own secret and command-injection checks are not affected. |
| `sql_injection` | boolean | `true` | When off, SQL injection patterns are not reported. |
| `xss` | boolean | `true` | When off, cross-site scripting patterns are not reported. |
| `path_traversal` | boolean | `true` | When off, path traversal patterns are not reported. |
| `hardcoded_secrets` | boolean | `true` | When off, secrets written into source are not reported by this check; the edit hook still checks for them. |
| `insecure_randomness` | boolean | `true` | When off, use of non-cryptographic random number generators for security values is not reported. |
| `command_injection` | boolean | `true` | When off, shell command injection patterns are not reported by this check; the edit hook still checks for them. |
| `block_on_severity` | "critical" \| "high" \| "medium" \| "low" | `"high"` | Lowest severity of security finding that is reported; findings below it are dropped. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: only a credential in a format only a real secret has (AWS access key, Stripe live key, sk-/ghp_-style keys, a private key block) blocks, and every other pattern is a note, since it cannot see whether its input is trusted. On: every reported pattern blocks, and so do a write through __proto__, constructor or prototype (ast-analysis) and a secret-named variable referenced in client code (frontend-secret-exposure). The healthcare, fintech, government and devsecops presets turn it on. |

## Frontend secret exposure

`gates.frontend_secret_exposure`

Finds server-side secrets referenced or embedded in files that are bundled for the browser. Teams adjust which paths count as frontend or server and which variable names count as secrets.

**Blocks:** Blocks a literal secret key; a secret-named variable reference is a note unless security.block is on

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the frontend secret exposure check on or off. |
| `block_on_severity` | "critical" \| "high" \| "medium" \| "low" | `"high"` | Lowest severity of exposure that is reported; findings below it are dropped, and medium or low findings that are reported do not block. |
| `check_process_env` | boolean | `true` | When on, secret-looking process.env references, including destructuring from process.env, are reported in frontend files. |
| `check_import_meta_env` | boolean | `true` | When on, secret-looking import.meta.env references are reported in frontend files. |
| `secret_env_name_patterns` | list of string | see below | Case-insensitive regular expressions; an environment variable whose name matches one is treated as a secret. |
| `safe_public_prefixes` | list of string | see below | Name prefixes that mark an environment variable as intentionally public, so it is never treated as a secret. |
| `frontend_path_patterns` | list of string | see below | Regular expressions matched against file paths that mark a file as definitely bundled for the browser, which makes a secret reference there critical rather than high; setting it replaces the built-in list. |
| `server_path_patterns` | list of string | see below | Regular expressions matched against file paths that mark a file as server-only so it is not scanned; entries are added to the built-in server paths rather than replacing them. |
| `allowlist_env_names` | list of string | `[]` | Exact environment variable names that are never treated as secrets. |

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.frontend_secret_exposure.secret_env_name_patterns</code></summary>

```json
[
  "(?:^|_)(?:secret|private)(?:_|$)",
  "(?:^|_)(?:token|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|signing|webhook)(?:_|$)",
  "(?:^|_)(?:db[_-]?url|database[_-]?url|connection[_-]?string)(?:_|$)"
]
```

</details>

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.frontend_secret_exposure.safe_public_prefixes</code></summary>

```json
[
  "NEXT_PUBLIC_",
  "VITE_",
  "PUBLIC_",
  "NUXT_PUBLIC_",
  "REACT_APP_"
]
```

</details>

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.frontend_secret_exposure.frontend_path_patterns</code></summary>

```json
[
  "(^|/)pages/(?!api/)",
  "(^|/)components/",
  "(^|/)src/components/",
  "(^|/)src/views/",
  "(^|/)src/app/",
  "(^|/)app/(?!api/)",
  "(^|/)views/",
  "(^|/)public/"
]
```

</details>

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.frontend_secret_exposure.server_path_patterns</code></summary>

```json
[
  "(^|/)pages/api/",
  "(^|/)src/pages/api/",
  "(^|/)app/api/",
  "(^|/)src/app/api/",
  "\\.server\\.(?:ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$"
]
```

</details>

## Duplicated functions across files

`gates.duplication_drift`

Finds JavaScript, TypeScript and Python functions whose bodies are exact or near-identical copies in different files. Teams tune the similarity and minimum size when small, intentionally parallel functions are reported.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the cross-file duplicated-function check on or off. |
| `similarity_threshold` | number | `0.8` | Structural similarity, from 0 to 1, above which two functions in different files are reported as near-duplicates; raise it to report only closer copies. |
| `min_body_lines` | number | `5` | Minimum function body length, in lines, for a function to be compared; raise it to ignore small helpers. |

## Imports that do not exist

`gates.hallucinated_imports`

Reports imports of files or packages that cannot be resolved in the project or its declared dependencies. Teams add ignore patterns for asset or generated imports a bundler resolves.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the unresolvable-import check on or off. |
| `ignore_patterns` | list of string | see below | Regular expressions matched against an import's specifier; matching imports are never reported, which suits assets and generated modules a bundler resolves. |

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.hallucinated_imports.ignore_patterns</code></summary>

```json
[
  "\\.css$",
  "\\.scss$",
  "\\.less$",
  "\\.svg$",
  "\\.png$",
  "\\.jpg$",
  "\\.json$",
  "\\.wasm$",
  "\\.graphql$",
  "\\.gql$"
]
```

</details>

## Inconsistent error handling

`gates.inconsistent_error_handling`

Reports an error type that is caught and handled in more distinct ways than allowed across two or more files. Teams raise the limits when varied handling is deliberate.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the inconsistent error-handling check on or off. |
| `max_strategies_per_type` | number | `2` | Number of distinct handling strategies allowed for one caught error type before it is reported; raise it to tolerate more variety. |
| `min_occurrences` | number | `3` | Minimum number of catch blocks for an error type before its handling is compared; raise it to ignore rarely caught types. |
| `ignore_empty_catches` | boolean | `false` | When on, empty catch blocks do not count as a handling strategy, so swallowed errors no longer push a type over the limit. |

## Quality drop within a long file

`gates.context_window_artifacts`

Compares the top and bottom halves of long files and reports files whose bottom half is markedly worse (fewer comments, longer functions, shorter names, less error handling, more empty blocks or TODOs). Teams tune the thresholds to make it more or less sensitive.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the within-file quality-drop check on or off. |
| `min_file_lines` | number | `180` | Minimum file length, in lines, for a file to be analysed; shorter files are skipped. |
| `degradation_threshold` | number | `0.55` | Degradation score, from 0 to 1, a file must reach to be reported; lower it to report milder drops. |
| `signals_required` | number | `4` | Number of separate degradation signals a file must show to be reported; lower it to make the check more sensitive. |

## Async and error-handling safety

`gates.promise_safety`

Reports promise chains without a catch, async functions that never await, HTTP calls without error handling and, optionally, unguarded JSON parsing, across JS/TS, Python, Go, Ruby and C#. Teams switch off individual patterns that do not fit their codebase.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the async and error-handling safety check on or off. |
| `check_unhandled_then` | boolean | `true` | Reports JavaScript and TypeScript .then() chains that have no .catch() and are not inside a try block. |
| `check_unsafe_parse` | boolean | `false` | Reports JSON parsing outside error handling in each supported language; off by default because it cannot tell trusted input from untrusted input. Test files, in any language, are never reported: there an uncaught parse error is the test failing. |
| `check_async_without_await` | boolean | `true` | Reports async functions that never use await, in JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and C#. |
| `check_unsafe_fetch` | boolean | `true` | Reports HTTP calls (such as fetch or axios) made without error handling or a status check. |
| `ignore_patterns` | list of string | `[]` | Regular expressions matched against file paths; matching files are not scanned by this check. |

## Calls to standard-library APIs that do not exist

`gates.phantom_apis`

Reports calls to methods that do not exist on known standard-library modules in Node.js, Python, Go, C#, Java and Kotlin. Teams turn off a language or exclude files that define look-alike APIs.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the non-existent standard-library API check on or off. |
| `check_node` | boolean | `true` | Includes JavaScript and TypeScript files, checked against Node.js built-in modules. |
| `check_python` | boolean | `true` | Includes Python files, checked against the Python standard library. |
| `check_go` | boolean | `true` | Includes Go files, checked against known non-existent Go standard-library calls. |
| `check_csharp` | boolean | `true` | Includes C# files, checked against known non-existent .NET APIs. |
| `check_java` | boolean | `true` | Includes Java and Kotlin files, checked against known non-existent JDK APIs. |
| `ignore_patterns` | list of string | `[]` | Regular expressions matched against file paths; matching files are not scanned by this check. |

## Deprecated and insecure APIs

`gates.deprecated_apis`

Reports use of deprecated or removed standard-library and web APIs, with security-deprecated ones reported separately at a higher severity. Teams turn off a language or decide whether security deprecations block.

**Blocks:** A note by default; blocks on security-deprecated APIs only when block_security_deprecated is on

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the deprecated and insecure API check on or off. |
| `check_node` | boolean | `true` | Includes JavaScript and TypeScript files; turning it off also skips the web API checks, which run on the same files. |
| `check_python` | boolean | `true` | Includes Python files, checked against Python deprecations and removals. |
| `check_web` | boolean | `true` | Checks JavaScript and TypeScript files for deprecated browser APIs and with statements; has no effect when check_node is off. |
| `check_go` | boolean | `true` | Includes Go files, checked against deprecated Go standard-library APIs. |
| `check_csharp` | boolean | `true` | Includes C# files, checked against deprecated .NET APIs. |
| `check_java` | boolean | `true` | Includes Java files, checked against deprecated JDK APIs. |
| `block_security_deprecated` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: APIs deprecated for security reasons are shown as notes, since deprecated is not always vulnerable (md5 for a cache key, shell=True with a constant). On: they are reported as critical and block. |
| `ignore_patterns` | list of string | `[]` | Regular expressions matched against file paths; matching files are not scanned by this check. |

## Weak tests

`gates.test_quality`

Reports tests that are empty, assert nothing, assert a tautology, rely on too many mocks, or are async without awaiting. Teams adjust the mock limit or switch off individual patterns.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the weak-test check on or off. |
| `check_empty_tests` | boolean | `true` | Reports tests with an empty body or with code but no assertion. |
| `check_tautological` | boolean | `true` | Reports assertions that can never fail, such as comparing a value with itself. |
| `check_mock_heavy` | boolean | `true` | Reports tests that set up more mocks than max_mocks_per_test. |
| `check_assertion_free_async` | boolean | `true` | Reports JavaScript and TypeScript async tests that assert without ever awaiting. |
| `max_mocks_per_test` | number | `5` | Number of mocks a single test may set up before check_mock_heavy reports it. |

## Agent memory and rules files

`gates.governance`

On the per-edit hook, checks agent writes to native memory and rules files (CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules and similar), optionally refusing them, and always scans their content for credentials. Teams turn on enforcement to route agent memory through Rigour.

**Blocks:** Edit hook only: not part of check or review

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns all memory and rules-file governance on the edit hook on or off, including the credential scan of those files. |
| `enforce_memory` | boolean | `false` | Reports a critical finding when an agent writes to a protected memory path, telling it to use rigour_remember; takes effect only while block_native_memory is also on. |
| `enforce_skills` | boolean | `false` | Reports a critical finding when an agent writes to a protected skills or rules path. |
| `block_native_memory` | boolean | `true` | Must be on, together with enforce_memory, for writes to protected memory paths to be reported; turning it off allows them. |
| `protected_memory_paths` | list of string | see below | Glob patterns for agent memory files that enforce_memory protects and whose content is scanned for credentials. |
| `protected_skills_paths` | list of string | see below | Glob patterns for agent skills and rules files that enforce_skills protects and whose content is scanned for credentials. |
| `exempt_paths` | list of string | see below | Glob patterns for files that governance never checks, such as Rigour's own hook configuration. |

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.governance.protected_memory_paths</code></summary>

```json
[
  "CLAUDE.md",
  ".claude/CLAUDE.md",
  ".clinerules",
  ".clinerules/**",
  ".windsurf/memories/**",
  ".github/copilot-instructions.md"
]
```

</details>

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.governance.protected_skills_paths</code></summary>

```json
[
  ".claude/skills/**",
  ".claude/rules/**",
  ".claude/commands/**",
  ".cursorrules",
  ".cursor/rules/**",
  ".cursor/prompts/**",
  ".cline/rules/**",
  ".windsurf/rules/**",
  ".windsurfrules",
  ".github/instructions/**",
  "copilot-instructions.md"
]
```

</details>

<details><summary>Default of <code>gates.governance.exempt_paths</code></summary>

```json
[
  ".claude/settings.json",
  ".cursor/hooks.json",
  ".windsurf/hooks.json"
]
```

</details>

## Unindexed Supabase reads

`gates.unindexed_reads`

Reports a supabase-js read whose table, as the repository's SQL migrations define it, has no index that can serve the read's filters or sort. Off by default; teams with Supabase migrations in the repository turn it on.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns the unindexed Supabase read check on or off. |
| `migrations` | list of string | `[]` | Glob patterns for the SQL migration files to replay, each directory as its own database; when empty, every .sql file under a migrations folder is used. |

## Deprecated npm dependencies

`gates.deprecated_dependencies`

Reports package.json dependencies whose installed version npm marks deprecated, by asking the registry (answers cached for a day). Off by default because it sends package names and versions to the registry.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns the deprecated npm dependency check on, which sends package names and installed versions to the registry. |
| `registry` | string | none | Base URL of the npm registry to ask about deprecations, for teams behind a private registry or mirror; npm's public registry is used when unset. |

## Unused exports

`gates.unused_exports`

Reports exports a change adds that no other non-test file imports. Teams list export names that a framework or tool loads by name.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the unused-export check on or off. |
| `allow` | list of string | `[]` | Export names, matched exactly, that are never reported because a framework or tool loads them by name. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Make an unused export block. Off by default: it is reported as a note, since teams often approve exports kept for tests or for another export's signature. |

## Costly query shapes

`gates.query_patterns`

Reports offset paging inside a loop and time windows read with a lower bound but no upper bound, on lines a change adds. Teams turn it off if they do not use query builders.

**Blocks:** Notes by default; block: true makes them block

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the offset-paging and unbounded-time-window checks on or off. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: an offset-paged loop or an open-ended time window is a note, since a small or caller-bounded table is fine. On: they block. |

## Half-finished changes

`gates.change_sweep`

Reports a fix applied at some sites while the old condition remains elsewhere, a prop added to some sibling component mounts but not others, and accumulators copied on every loop step. Teams turn it off as a whole.

**Blocks:** Notes by default; block: true makes them block

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the partial-fix, partial-wiring and quadratic-copy checks on or off together. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: a partial fix, a prop wired into some sibling mounts only, or a copied accumulator is a note, since the difference may be deliberate. On: they block. |

## Redundant code found with the TypeScript checker

`gates.redundancy`

Uses the project's TypeScript program to report redundant null filters, nullable row types for columns the query filters non-null, optional members every caller supplies, and properties written but never read. Teams list cross-service type files and the SQL migrations that define column nullability.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines; the NOT NULL column note is advisory

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the TypeScript-checker redundancy checks on or off; they run only when the change touches non-test TypeScript files. |
| `wire_contracts` | list of string | `[]` | Glob patterns for files whose types another service reads, so their properties are never reported as written but never read. |
| `schema_migrations` | list of string | `["supabase/migrations"]` | Folders of SQL migrations (relative, absolute or starting with ~/, possibly in another repository) replayed in file-name order to learn which columns are NOT NULL; missing folders are skipped. |

## Parameters optional only for tests

`gates.optional_params`

Reports a parameter a change adds as optional that every non-test caller passes. Teams turn it off if they keep such parameters optional on purpose.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the optional-only-for-tests parameter check on or off. |

## Duplicate functions in the change

`gates.duplicate_functions`

Reports a function a change adds or edits whose body is the same as another function's in the files the change touched. Teams turn it off as a whole.

**Blocks:** Notes by default; block: true makes them block

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the duplicate-function check on the changed files on or off. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: a duplicated function body is a note, since generated code and deliberate per-module copies exist. On: it blocks. |

## Files nothing uses

`gates.orphan_files`

Reports code files a change adds that nothing imports, runs or names in package.json, CI or config. Teams list globs for files a tool loads by path.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the unused-new-file check on or off. |
| `allow` | list of string | `[]` | Glob patterns for files that are never reported because a tool loads them by path. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Make an orphaned file block. Off by default: it is reported as a note. |

## The team's lessons, compiled into checks

`gates.compiled_lessons`

Runs the checks a person compiled from verified review lessons (rigour learn-reviews --compile, then --approve-check): a symbol a lesson forbids, or one it requires a partner for, on a changed line. Only person-approved checks run.

**Blocks:** Never by default; block: true makes them block

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the compiled-lesson checks on or off. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Make a compiled lesson's finding block. Off by default: it is reported as a note. |

## Migrations added out of order

`gates.migration_order`

Reports a SQL migration a change adds that sorts before the newest migration already on the base in the same directory. Off by default; teams whose migration runner applies files in name order turn it on.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns the out-of-order migration check on or off. |
| `dirs` | list of string | `["**/supabase/migrations"]` | Glob patterns matched against the directory of each added .sql file; only migrations in matching directories are checked. |

## Proven semantic bugs

`gates.semantic_bugs`

Runs type-aware rules on JavaScript and TypeScript that trace a value from where it enters to where it causes a defect, and report only what they can prove. Teams can restrict it to named rules or opt in to candidate rules.

**Blocks:** Blocks on changed lines

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the proven semantic-bug rules on or off. |
| `rules` | list of string | none | Rule ids to run, including opt-in candidate rules and learned rules as learned/<id>; when set, only the named rules run, and when unset the default rules plus the repository's learned rules run. |

## Runaway side effects

`gates.side_effect_analysis`

Reports timers never cleared, spawned processes without lifecycle handling, I/O loops with no exit, retries without a limit, file watchers that trigger themselves, resource leaks, unbounded recursion and auto-restart loops. Teams switch off individual patterns or exclude files.

**Blocks:** Notes by default; with block: true the critical patterns (unbounded I/O loops, circular triggers, auto-restart) block

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the runaway side-effect check on or off. |
| `check_unbounded_timers` | boolean | `true` | Reports interval timers that are never cleared. |
| `check_unbounded_loops` | boolean | `true` | Reports loops that perform I/O with no exit condition or delay. |
| `check_process_lifecycle` | boolean | `true` | Reports spawned child processes with no exit handling, wait or kill. |
| `check_recursive_depth` | boolean | `true` | Reports recursive functions with no base case before the recursive call. |
| `check_resource_lifecycle` | boolean | `true` | Reports opened resources, such as files or connections, that are never closed. |
| `check_retry_without_limit` | boolean | `true` | Reports retry loops that catch an error and try again with no attempt limit. |
| `check_circular_triggers` | boolean | `true` | Reports file watchers that write to a path they are watching. |
| `check_auto_restart` | boolean | `true` | Reports code that restarts a process on exit with no limit. |
| `block` | boolean | `false` | Off by default: every finding is a note, since servers, consumers and daemons loop forever by design and a limit set elsewhere is not seen. On: the critical patterns (unbounded I/O loop, circular trigger, auto-restart) block. |
| `ignore_patterns` | list of string | `[]` | Regular expressions matched against file paths; matching files are not scanned by this check. |

## Style drift from project conventions

`gates.style_drift`

In a Git checkout, compares each changed or new file with the naming and error-handling conventions of its language in the code committed on the main branch, read fresh on every run; nothing is cached. Outside Git, builds a per-language baseline file on the first full scan and compares against it. Teams tune the deviation threshold, the sample size or (outside Git) the baseline file.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the style-drift check on or off. |
| `deviation_threshold` | number | `0.25` | Fraction, from 0 to 1, by which a file's naming or error-handling style must differ from the project baseline to be reported; raise it to report only larger deviations. |
| `sample_size` | number | `100` | Maximum number of files per language the conventions are read from: committed files on the main branch in a Git checkout, else those of the first full scan. |
| `baseline_path` | string | `".rigour/style-baseline.json"` | Outside Git only: path, relative to the repository root, where the style baseline is stored and read; delete the file to rebuild the baseline on the next full scan. In a Git checkout it is never read or written. |

## Logic changes in edited functions

`gates.logic_drift`

Compares changed functions with their version on the main branch (or a local baseline file outside Git) and reports comparison-operator changes and, optionally, return and branch count changes. Teams opt in to the extra signals.

**Blocks:** Advisory: never blocks

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Turns the logic-drift check on or off. |
| `baseline_path` | string | `".rigour/logic-baseline.json"` | Path, relative to the repository root, of the local function baseline used only when the project is not a Git repository. |
| `track_operators` | boolean | `true` | Reports changes to comparison operators in an edited function, such as >= becoming >. |
| `track_branches` | boolean | `false` | Reports a change of two or more in the number of branches in an edited function. |
| `track_returns` | boolean | `false` | Reports a change in the number of return statements in an edited function. |

## Model review

`gates.deep`

Tuning for model review: a check or review started with --deep, --pro, --max or an API key ([Model review](./MODEL_REVIEW.md)). Whether it runs, and which model and provider, come from those flags and your own settings, never from this file.

**Blocks:** Verified model findings fail the check.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_tokens` | number | none | The most tokens the model may write per model review call; lower values cut cost and may truncate answers. |
| `temperature` | number | `0.1` | The sampling temperature for model review calls; higher values make the model's answers less repeatable. |
| `timeout_ms` | number | none | How long, in milliseconds, a single model review model call may run before it is abandoned. |
| `budget_ms` | number | none | A time limit, in milliseconds, for the whole model review of a change; files not started before it runs out are reported as skipped instead of reviewed. |
| `agentic` | boolean | none | Set to false to stop a cloud model from reading other repository files while it reviews a change, so it sees only what Rigour sends it. |
| `repo_rules` | boolean | none | When true, the model review, the agent review list and the stop hook's end-of-task question include the rules from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and Cursor rules that name what the change touches. The reviewer (review.reviewer) always checks the repository's rules, whatever this says. |
| `review_lessons` | "verified" \| "all" \| "off" | none | Which of the team's past review lessons raise a function's risk, are shown to the reviewer, and are put to the agent once at the stop hook: lessons (promoted on evidence), all of them including candidates (never one only review bots raised), or none (off). |
| `intent_checks` | boolean | `false` | When true, a scoped model review also asks the model intent questions at places the engine has proven read an optional value with no fallback. |

## Risk router

`gates.deep.router`

Picks which changed functions get model attention: the riskiest ones, in cloud model reviews and in the agent review list.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | none | Set to false to send every changed file to the cloud model instead of only the riskiest changed functions. |
| `min_score` | number | none | The risk score a changed function needs to go to the model or onto the agent review list; functions below it get the deterministic checks only. |
| `max_functions` | number | none | The most changed functions sent to the model, or listed for agent review, per change; the highest-risk ones are kept. |

## Model review categories

`gates.deep.checks`

Which categories the model is asked about in a whole-repository model review. A review of a change does not use them.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `solid` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about SOLID principle violations in a whole-repository model review. |
| `dry` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about duplicated logic in a whole-repository model review. |
| `design_patterns` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about design anti-patterns (god classes, feature envy, long parameter lists and similar) in a whole-repository model review. |
| `language_idioms` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about language-specific anti-patterns, naming conventions and dead code in a whole-repository model review. |
| `error_handling` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about error handling (empty catches, swallowed errors, missing checks) in a whole-repository model review. |
| `test_quality` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about weak or missing tests in a whole-repository model review. |
| `architecture` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about layer violations, circular dependencies and API design in a whole-repository model review. |
| `code_smells` | boolean | `true` | Set to false to stop asking the model about code smells (complex conditionals, magic numbers, hardcoded config) in a whole-repository model review. |

## Agent hooks

`hooks`

Settings for the hooks Rigour installs into coding agents. Installation itself is driven by rigour hooks init flags; of these keys only require_review_ack changes behaviour.

**Blocks:** With require_review_ack, the agent cannot finish until risky functions are acknowledged.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `require_review_ack` | boolean | `false` | When true, the agent stop hook holds the agent until each risky changed function has been acknowledged with rigour_review_ack. |

## Output

`output`

Where rigour check writes its JSON report, and where explain, export-audit, the MCP server and the stop hook look for it.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `report_path` | string | `"rigour-report.json"` | The file, relative to the repository root, that rigour check writes its JSON report to and that other commands read it from. |

## Review

`review`

How rigour review, the rigour_review tool, the stop hook and the push hook decide a verdict.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `include_heuristics` | boolean | `false` | When true, heuristic findings (size, complexity, guessed intent) can decide the verdict and block, instead of only findings that prove a defect. |
| `show_preexisting` | boolean | `false` | When true, a review also reports rule findings the base commit already had, instead of only those the change introduced. |
| `coverage` | boolean | `false` | When the model reviewer runs, it accounts for every changed unit (a function, or a hunk named by its enclosing code): a finding, or what it checked and why it holds. A unit it leaves out gets one follow-up run, then is reported as not reviewed, never passed. At most 25 units per review, riskiest and largest first; the rest are counted as not offered. |
| `review_points` | boolean | `false` | When the model reviewer runs, it also raises review points: what a careful reviewer would ask to change though nothing goes wrong today (one job done twice, a cheaper path on the code's frequent path, a lock or copy it does not need, a branch that forgets an error or callback). Never a block. At most five per review, the most confident first; the rest are counted. Each needs a quote Rigour finds at the line it names. |
| `goal` | "off" \| "on" \| "required" | `"off"` | Checks a change against the goal its pull request's description declares (Scope, Out of scope, Done when): off, on, or required, which stops a person, RIGOUR_GOAL or --no-goal turning it off (team; a person sets goal in settings.json). |
| `github_account` | string | none | The gh account whose token Rigour uses to read the pull request and its reviews, and that rigour learn-reviews reads past reviews as; ignored when GH_TOKEN is set, and RIGOUR_GITHUB_ACCOUNT is used when this is unset. |

## The reviewer

`review.reviewer`

The reviewer that runs your own installed coding-agent CLIs (claude, cursor, codex) headless against a change, from one judge up to a cross-vendor panel. A person may override some keys in their own settings; the team's rigour.yml can set a floor they cannot go below. See [The reviewer](./REVIEWER.md).

**Blocks:** Open findings, or an unavailable required review, block a push when on_push is wait.

| Setting | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Runs the model reviewer at push; a person cannot turn it off when the team sets panel: required or mode_required (team or person). |
| `on_push` | "background" \| "wait" \| "off" | `"background"` | At push, background starts the review without holding the push, wait holds the push for its verdict, and off reviews only when asked with rigour review --reviewer (team only). |
| `reviewers` | list of string | `["claude"]` | The agent CLIs to use as judges, in order of preference, from claude, cursor and codex (team or person). |
| `mode` | "single" \| "cross" \| "full" | `"single"` | How many judges review: single uses the first installed reviewer, cross prefers a vendor that did not write the commits, full uses one per vendor and merges their verdicts (team or person). |
| `model` | string | none | The model the claude reviewer runs, unless models names one for claude (team only). |
| `models` | map of string | `{}` | A model per reviewer name, passed to that agent CLI (team or person). |
| `timeout_ms` | number | `900000` | How long, in milliseconds, each agent CLI run may take before it is stopped (team only). |
| `panel` | "off" \| "on" \| "required" | `"off"` | With two or more vendors, on makes judges cross-examine findings only one raised and block only on confirmed ones; required also stops anyone turning it off and makes a review without two vendors unavailable (a person may only switch it on or off) (team or person). |
| `mode_required` | boolean | `false` | When true, no person, environment variable or flag may review with fewer judges than the team's mode, and a run that cannot meet it is unavailable (team only). |
| `dismissals` | boolean | `false` | When true, people may dismiss a reviewer finding as not a bug and it is not reported again (team only). |
| `orchestrator` | "off" \| "on" \| "required" | `"off"` | Reviews only the parts a change needs, picked without a model, in one pass at the cost of one judge; a change over the judge's limit is split only with what the router already saved over its last 20 reviews, and a change with nothing for a model gets no run: off, on, or required, which stops a person, RIGOUR_REVIEWER_ORCHESTRATOR or --no-orchestrator turning it off and gives no verdict unless every part returns (team; a person sets orchestrator in settings.json). Experimental; max_runs_per_day and max_usd_per_day count every pass. |
| `panel_max_items` | number | `20` | The most findings cross-examined per panel review; the rest are shown as disputed (team only). |
| `max_runs_per_day` | number | none | A cap on agent runs per repository per local day, cross-examinations included; past it a review is skipped, or unavailable when the team requires the reviewer, and a person may only set a lower cap (team or person). |
| `max_usd_per_day` | number | none | A cap, in US dollars as reported by the agent CLIs, on reviewer spend per repository per local day; past it a review is skipped, or unavailable when the team requires the reviewer, and a person may only set a lower cap (team or person). |
| `judges` | 2 \| 3 | `2` | How many judges, each from a different vendor, a full or panel review uses (2 or 3), limited by the vendors installed; under a team floor a person cannot lower it (team or person). |
| `escalate` | "always" \| "risk" | `"always"` | With risk, a full or panel review uses one judge unless the change has a risky function, a human review exists or the run is rigour review --full; always uses every judge on every review; a team floor forces always (team or person). |
| `cross_models` | map of string | `{}` | A model per reviewer name used only for cross-examining disputed findings, so that narrower step can run on a cheaper model (team only). |
| `tiers.cheap` | map of string | `{}` | Cheap-model-first tiering, off by default and experimental (team only): a cheaper model per reviewer name, used for a change with no risk signal (no human reviews, carried items, migration, security finding, goal or risky function); anything else, and the retry of a cheap answer that is not a verdict, runs the team's model. Turns itself off when its reviews cost more on average than one judge would have. |
| `reasoning` | map of "low" \| "medium" \| "high" | `{}` | Reasoning effort per reviewer name where the judge takes one (codex, api): low, medium or high. A slow judge finishes sooner at a lower effort; measure before you rely on it (team only). |
| `api.url` | string | none | The API's base URL; /chat/completions is appended. |
| `api.model` | string | none | The model name the API expects. |
| `api.key_env` | string | `"RIGOUR_JUDGE_API_KEY"` | The environment variable holding the API key (default RIGOUR_JUDGE_API_KEY). The judge is installed only when it is set. |
| `api.vendor` | "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "google" \| "other" | none | The model's maker (anthropic, openai, google, other), used by cross and full modes to pair judges from different vendors; inferred from the model name when unset. |
| `api.max_turns` | number | `60` | Tool-call turns the judge may take before the review is unavailable (default 60). |
| `judge_env` | map of object | `{}` | Environment variables a judge's CLI must not see, per reviewer name, e.g. codex: { unset: [OPENAI_API_KEY] } when that variable holds a key meant for another service; RIGOUR_API_KEY is never passed to a judge (team only). |
